info.title: Terrain Viewer tile service
info.description:
## Quick start

Copy an address into QGIS (XYZ Tiles), MapLibre, CesiumJS or Blender. `{z}/{x}/{y}` stay as they are: the client fills them.

**Slope, Mapterhorn, XYZ tiles** (any mode of `/processes`, several comma-separated; the source id is the path segment after `/terrain-tiles/` (`/terrain-sources` lists them))

```text
http://localhost:3400/terrain-tiles/mapterhorn/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?modes=slope
```

**Sky-view factor, IGN RGE ALTI (France), XYZ tiles** (zoom 12 and finer; the first tiles of an area take a second or two)

```text
http://localhost:3400/terrain-tiles/custom-fr-ign-rgealti-highres/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?modes=svf
```

**A source given by its address (Terrarium tiles, a COG, a VRT, JSON)** (the query form, for anything that is not a library id)

```text
http://localhost:3400/terrain-tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?modes=hillshade&terrainSource=https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png
```

**Cesium terrain (quantized mesh), Mapterhorn: the layer.json** (CesiumJS, Blender's OGC 3D Tiles add-on as a *Quantized-mesh terrain* entry; martini mesher, heights above the ellipsoid (geoid added))

```text
http://localhost:3400/quantized-mesh/mapterhorn/layer.json
```

**The same, meshed by delatin** (half the triangles, three times slower to make)

```text
http://localhost:3400/quantized-mesh/mapterhorn/layer.json?mesher=delatin
```

**Imagery: Esri Wayback of 2020, XYZ tiles** (dated imagery and the built-in basemaps by id: `/basemaps`)

```text
http://localhost:3400/basemap-tiles/wayback/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg?imageryDate=2020-01-01
```

**A picture of a box** (west,south,east,north; `.tif` with one mode for its values)

```text
http://localhost:3400/bbox/7.6,45.95,7.7,46/800x600.png?terrainSource=mapterhorn&modes=hillshade,contours
```

**A colour ramp as a picture** (a legend; `orientation=vertical`; the ids: `/colorramps`)

```text
http://localhost:3400/colorramps/slope-plantopo.png?width=256&height=16
```

**The STAC Item of a tile** (any raster export's address plus `.stac.json`)

```text
http://localhost:3400/terrain-tiles/mapterhorn/12/2133/1449.png.stac.json?modes=slope
```

**Building shadows from Overture's buildings, XYZ tiles** (zoom 13 and finer; `buildingShadowSource`: an id of `/building-sources`, or a PMTiles, TileJSON or `{z}/{x}/{y}` address with `buildingShadowLayer` and `buildingShadowHeightField`)

```text
http://localhost:3400/terrain-tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?modes=buildingShadows&buildingShadowSource=overture-buildings&illuminationDir=135&illuminationAlt=25
```

**The terrain sources, by id** (what `/terrain-tiles/{source}/...`, `/quantized-mesh/{source}/...` and `terrainSource` take; one with its description: `/terrain-sources/{id}`)

```text
http://localhost:3400/terrain-sources
```

**The modes, as OGC API - Processes** (each mode's settings: `/processes/{id}`)

```text
http://localhost:3400/processes
```

**Addresses.** A library id goes in the path, as `{source}`: `/terrain-tiles/{source}/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`, `/basemap-tiles/{source}/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg`, `/quantized-mesh/{source}/layer.json`. Anything else (a tile address, a COG, a VRT, a JSON configuration) goes in the query: `/terrain-tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?terrainSource=...`, `/basemap-tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.jpg?imageryUrl=...`, `/quantized-mesh/custom/layer.json?terrainSource=...` (`custom` in the path means the same everywhere). Both forms answer the same tile.

## About

What Terrain Viewer draws, as map tiles and as pictures of a viewport. Two engines draw them. The direct engine computes every 2D terrain mode in the server with the app's own code, reading the elevation with the app's own readers (tile pyramids, COG, VRT, WMS and WCS, LERC, quantized mesh, PMTiles, differences), in a fraction of a second. For everything else the app itself renders them in a headless browser, so every source it reads and every mode it computes comes out as in the app: a tile is drawn with the 2048 px block around it and the block is kept a week, so the first tile of a block takes seconds and its neighbours milliseconds. Web Mercator only.

The elevation modes are at `/terrain-tiles`, the imagery at `/basemap-tiles`, the terrain as Cesium meshes at `/quantized-mesh`. Each mode is described as an OGC API - Processes process at `/processes/{id}`: its settings with their types, ranges and defaults.

**How several modes stack.** `modes=a,b,c` draws them in one tile, in the map's order, never in the order written: bottom to top, `colorRelief`, `slope`, `aspect`, `tri`, `curvature`, `tpi`, `lrm`, `ndsm`, `roughness`, `shapeIndex`, `blobness`, `eigenRatio`, `orientation`, `svf`, `openness`, `localDominance`, `hillshade`, `matcap`, `phong`, `shadows`, `buildingShadows`, `isoline`, `graticules`, `moundDetector`, `planeSlicer`, `contours`. The last is on top (the contours over everything, the colour relief at the bottom). `/processes/{id}` gives each mode's place as `x-tv-stack-rank` (0 at the bottom).

**Opacity.** A mode's opacity is its own parameter (`slopeOpacity`, `svfOpacity`, `phongOpacity`, ... named in `x-tv-opacity-key`) times its panel group's (`terrainAnalysisOpacity`, `reliefVisualizationOpacity`, `lightingEffectsOpacity`, listed in `x-tv-group-opacity-keys`), each 0 to 1: `slopeOpacity=0.5&terrainAnalysisOpacity=0.4` draws the slope at 0.2. The group's opacity scales every mode of the group, each one separately (not the group flattened first).

**Blending.** Over the map's background (white, black with `theme=dark`, transparent with `background=none`), each layer is drawn source-over with that opacity. The shading layers are different: the hillshade is a half-transparent dark and light layer drawn over what is under it; Phong and matcap multiply the colours under them and add their highlight; the terrain and building shadows darken. In a GIS, stack them with a multiply blend (the QGIS project does). The overlays (contours, iso-line, graticule, mound markers, plane slicer) are lines and areas over everything.

**Defaults.** Without `modes`, the hillshade alone. Given without `hillshade`, the hillshade is off. A mode's group switch does not bring the group's default mode with it (asking for `aspect` does not also draw `slope`).

**Refused together.** `basemap` with a terrain mode on `/terrain-tiles` (400: ask `/basemap-tiles` for the imagery and stack the two in the client; `/render` draws them in one picture). Any terrain mode on `/basemap-tiles` (400). On `.pbf`/`.mvt`, any mode that is only a picture: only `contours`, `isoline`, `moundDetector`, `graticules` and `planeSlicer` are vector (400). On `.tif` and `encoding=`, more than one mode, or a mode without values (400). `engine=direct` with a mode or source only the browser draws (400). Otherwise any set of modes stacks.

tags.name: Visualization modes (OGC API – Processes)
tags.description: The modes as OGC API - Processes processes (OGC 18-062r2), with OGC API Common's landing page and conformance. `/processes` lists every mode with its settings; a process is run by asking for its tiles: its description links them.

tags.name: Terrain tiles
tags.description: `/terrain-tiles`: the elevation modes as XYZ raster tiles (`/terrain-sources` lists the sources by id), the overlays as vector tiles, a TileJSON and a QGIS project of them.

tags.name: Quantized mesh
tags.description: `/quantized-mesh`: any direct source as Cesium terrain (quantized-mesh-1.0) for CesiumJS, Cesium for Unreal or Unity and Blender. Give the client the layer.json; it asks for the tiles.

tags.name: Basemap tiles
tags.description: `/basemap-tiles`: the imagery under the terrain, as XYZ tiles, as the app draws it. Not only the historical imagery: the dated sources (Esri Wayback, Google Earth historical, Bing, HLS, EOX Sentinel-2, each with a date) and the app's built-in basemaps with a fixed address (Google, Bing Aerial, Esri, Mapbox, MapTiler, HERE), both by id in the path (`/basemaps` lists them), plus any XYZ or COG address in the query (`imageryUrl`). Drawn by the browser engine, except Google Earth historical, which the service builds itself. `/imagery-dates/{source}` lists a dated source's dates at a place.

tags.description: What can be named by id: colour ramps (and pictures of them), modes, and what a share link switches on.

tags.name: Viewport

tags.name: Values
tags.description: A mode's numbers before the colour ramp, in natural units: Float32 GeoTIFF for analysis (GDAL, QGIS, rasterio, numpy), or packed in a PNG for a web map.

get.summary: A mode's values as a Float32 GeoTIFF tile
get.description: One band of 32-bit floats, EPSG:3857, georeferenced, NaN where there is no data: the values the app colours, before its ramp, in natural units (the unit in the `x-tv-value-unit` header and in `/processes/{id}`). 256 px; `{y}@2x` or `tilesize=512` for 512. The same tile as a PNG for a web map: `.png?modes=slope&encoding=terrarium` (or `terrainrgb`), the values multiplied by `valueScale` (default 1) and packed as an elevation, so MapLibre's raster-dem or a few lines of numpy read them back; `valueScale` keeps small values (curvature) above the packing's step (Terrarium 1/256, Terrain-RGB 0.1). Computed by the direct engine only. Browsers do not display TIFF: Scalar's test request answers "Preview unavailable" and offers the file to download. **Provenance:** the same address plus `.stac.json` (same query) answers a STAC Item of this export (STAC 1.1.0, Processing extension v1.2.0: its footprint, the source it was derived from, the process and parameters as executed, the software version), and the answer names it in a `Link: <...>; rel="describedby"` header.

parameters.description: The side of the tile in pixels.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: With `.png` in place of `.tif`: the values packed in a PNG as an elevation would be.

parameters.description: With `encoding`: the factor the values are multiplied by before packing.

parameters.name: compression
parameters.description: Deflate with the floating-point predictor (GDAL's PREDICTOR=3), lossless: about a quarter of the size for elevation, half for slope, two thirds for curvature or svf, for 2 to 6 ms a tile. `none` for a reader without deflate.

get.description: What `/terrain-tiles/{source}/...`, `/quantized-mesh/{source}/...` and `terrainSource` take: every elevation source the app knows, the built-in ones and the library. Each with its type, its tile address when it is a plain pyramid (`url`), the raw elevation's address of a COG, VRT or raw WMS, WCS or ArcGIS image service (`address`, what GDAL can open), its zoom range and extent, and the engine that can draw it.

get.description: One entry of `/terrain-sources`, with its description.

get.summary: One XYZ tile of the elevation modes
get.description: A 256 px Web Mercator tile of the modes computed from the elevation (every mode but `basemap`), stacked as described under `modes`. A library source can go in the path instead: `/terrain-tiles/{source}/{z}/{x}/{y}.{format}`. For 512 px write `{y}@2x` in the address or add `tilesize=512`. The camera is the tile's: `lat`, `lng`, `zoom`, `pitch` and `bearing` are not read. The imagery is at `/basemap-tiles`. titiler's `url` (the source) and `algorithm` (one mode) are read; its address `/tiles/WebMercatorQuad/...` was removed on 2026-11-25 (404). **Provenance:** the same address plus `.stac.json` (same query) answers a STAC Item of this export (STAC 1.1.0, Processing extension v1.2.0: its footprint, the source it was derived from, the process and parameters as executed, the software version), and the answer names it in a `Link: <...>; rel="describedby"` header.

parameters.name: tilesize
parameters.description: The side of the tile in pixels.

parameters.name: terrainSource
parameters.description: The elevation source: an id from `/terrain-sources`, the address of Terrarium tiles, of a COG (`.tif`) or of a VRT (`.vrt`), or a configuration as JSON with the fields of a library entry, `{"url": ..., "type": "terrarium" | "terrainrgb" | "cog" | "vrt" | "wms-raw" | "lerc" | "quantized-mesh" | "tilejson", "maxzoom": ...}`. Unset: Mapterhorn. `url` is read as the same parameter.

parameters.name: ndsmSubtrahend
parameters.description: With the `ndsm` mode: the terrain source subtracted from `terrainSource` (an id, a tile address or a JSON configuration, as for `terrainSource`; not itself a difference). `ndsmInvert=true` subtracts the other way, `ndsmOffset` (metres) is added to every difference. Without it the `ndsm` mode draws nothing and its values are refused with a 400; the second source is read only while the mode is drawn.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: Who draws. `direct`: computed in the server from elevation tiles, in a fraction of a second, for the modes and parameters `/algorithms` lists as direct on a source `/terrain-sources` lists as direct. `browser`: the app in a headless browser, every source and mode, seconds. `auto` (the default) takes direct when it can. The answer's `x-tv-engine` header says which drew it, `x-tv-engine-why` why not direct.

get.summary: A source as Cesium terrain: its layer.json
get.description: The layer.json a Cesium terrain client reads first (CesiumJS `CesiumTerrainProvider.fromUrl`, Cesium for Unreal or Unity, Blender add-ons that read Cesium terrain): TileJSON 2.1.0, `format: quantized-mesh-1.0`, `scheme: tms`, `projection: EPSG:4326` (two tiles at level 0), `available` level by level (whole at level 0, the source's bounds below), down to the level as fine as the source (its deepest 256 px Web Mercator zoom, less one), `extensions: [octvertexnormals]` and the source's attribution. The tile template keeps the query given (`mesher`, `heights`, ...). Heights are above the WGS84 ellipsoid by default, as quantized-mesh expects (see `heights`). Any source the direct engine reads (`/terrain-sources`, engine `direct`): Terrarium and Terrain-RGB pyramids, COG, VRT, WMS, LERC, PMTiles, with the same API keys as `/terrain-tiles`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: An id from `/terrain-sources`, or `custom` with the source in `terrainSource` (an address or a JSON configuration).

parameters.name: terrainSource
parameters.description: With `custom`: the source's address or configuration, as for `/terrain-tiles`.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: The mesh's vertical error, as a share of Cesium's geometric error of the level (77 km at level 0, halved each level: 4.7 m at level 14, times 0.5 is 2.35 m). Smaller for a finer mesh (more triangles), larger for a lighter one.

parameters.name: mesher
parameters.description: `martini` (the default since 2026-11-25): a right-triangulated irregular network on the 257 x 257 grid, 5 to 15 ms a tile, about twice the triangles of delatin. `delatin`: Delaunay refinement, about 45% fewer triangles and bytes for the same error, 20 to 55 ms a tile (three times slower): for a scene where bytes matter more than the time to make them.

parameters.name: heights
parameters.description: The vertical datum of the heights. `ellipsoidal` (the default): above the WGS84 ellipsoid, what quantized-mesh means and what CesiumJS, Cesium for Unreal and Unity and Cesium World Terrain use; the sources give heights above sea level (orthometric), so the EGM96 geoid's height N is added (h = H + N: about +45 m in Paris, +51 m in the Alps, from -106 m south of India to +85 m in New Guinea). Without it the ground sits N metres too low under 3D Tiles, photogrammetry and GNSS data. `orthometric`: the source's own heights above sea level, for a client that places everything on the geoid (a local scene in metres above sea level). An ellipsoidal source (`cesium`) is not shifted again: with `orthometric` it has N taken off. EGM96 15' grid, bilinear (NGA, public domain), shipped with the service.

parameters.name: maxTriangles
parameters.description: delatin only: the most triangles a tile gets. The mesh stops refining there, worst points first, even above `error`. The default only bounds noisy or very fine sources (Mapterhorn's Alps need 7,000 to 15,000 a tile); lower it to keep a 3D scene light.

parameters.name: extensions
parameters.description: The extensions to write, for a client that sets no `Accept: application/vnd.quantized-mesh;extensions=octvertexnormals` header (CesiumJS sets it when asked for vertex normals).

parameters.description: With the `ndsm` mode: the terrain source subtracted from `terrainSource` (an id, a tile address or a JSON configuration, as for `terrainSource`; not itself a difference). `ndsmInvert=true` subtracts the other way, `ndsmOffset` (metres) is added to every difference. parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: Who draws. `direct`: computed in the server from elevation tiles, in a fraction of a second, for the modes and parameters `/algorithms` lists as direct on a source `/terrain-sources` lists as direct. `browser`: the app in a headless browser, every source and mode, seconds. `auto` (the default) takes direct when it can. The answer's `x-tv-engine` header says which drew it, `x-tv-engine-why` why not direct.

parameters.name: background
parameters.description: `none`: no white (or black) map background, a transparent PNG to stack layers in a GIS. Direct engine only; the browser's tiles keep the map's background.

parameters.name: modes
parameters.description:
The modes to draw, comma-separated (`style: form, explode: false`). `algorithm` is read as the same parameter. Each mode is a process: `/processes/{id}` lists its settings.

**How several modes stack.** `modes=a,b,c` draws them in one tile, in the map's order, never in the order written: bottom to top, `colorRelief`, `slope`, `aspect`, `tri`, `curvature`, `tpi`, `lrm`, `ndsm`, `roughness`, `shapeIndex`, `blobness`, `eigenRatio`, `orientation`, `svf`, `openness`, `localDominance`, `hillshade`, `matcap`, `phong`, `shadows`, `buildingShadows`, `isoline`, `graticules`, `moundDetector`, `planeSlicer`, `contours`. The last is on top (the contours over everything, the colour relief at the bottom). `/processes/{id}` gives each mode's place as `x-tv-stack-rank` (0 at the bottom).

**Opacity.** A mode's opacity is its own parameter (`slopeOpacity`, `svfOpacity`, `phongOpacity`, ... named in `x-tv-opacity-key`) times its panel group's (`terrainAnalysisOpacity`, `reliefVisualizationOpacity`, `lightingEffectsOpacity`, listed in `x-tv-group-opacity-keys`), each 0 to 1: `slopeOpacity=0.5&terrainAnalysisOpacity=0.4` draws the slope at 0.2. The group's opacity scales every mode of the group, each one separately (not the group flattened first).

**Blending.** Over the map's background (white, black with `theme=dark`, transparent with `background=none`), each layer is drawn source-over with that opacity. The shading layers are different: the hillshade is a half-transparent dark and light layer drawn over what is under it; Phong and matcap multiply the colours under them and add their highlight; the terrain and building shadows darken. In a GIS, stack them with a multiply blend (the QGIS project does). The overlays (contours, iso-line, graticule, mound markers, plane slicer) are lines and areas over everything.

**Defaults.** Without `modes`, the hillshade alone. Given without `hillshade`, the hillshade is off. A mode's group switch does not bring the group's default mode with it (asking for `aspect` does not also draw `slope`).

**Refused together.** `basemap` with a terrain mode on `/terrain-tiles` (400: ask `/basemap-tiles` for the imagery and stack the two in the client; `/render` draws them in one picture). Any terrain mode on `/basemap-tiles` (400). On `.pbf`/`.mvt`, any mode that is only a picture: only `contours`, `isoline`, `moundDetector`, `graticules` and `planeSlicer` are vector (400). On `.tif` and `encoding=`, more than one mode, or a mode without values (400). `engine=direct` with a mode or source only the browser draws (400). Otherwise any set of modes stacks.

get.summary: One mode, as a process description
get.description:
The mode's settings as `inputs`, each with a JSON Schema (`type`, `enum`, `default`, `minimum`/`maximum` for opacities) and the app's URL parameter (`x-tv-url-param`, `x-tv-type`, `x-tv-role`: setting, opacity, group-opacity or common). `outputs`: `image` (image/png, image/jpeg), `values` for a mode with values (Float32 GeoTIFF, `x-tv-unit`, `x-tv-display-range`), `vectorTile` for an overlay. What OGC has no slot for: `x-tv-group` (its panel groups), `x-tv-form`, `x-tv-shading`, `x-tv-stack-rank`, `x-tv-opacity-key`, `x-tv-group-opacity-keys`, `x-tv-switches` (the app's show* parameters), `x-tv-has-values`, `x-tv-values` (unit, description, the typical range the QGIS plugin's grey ramp starts with).

**Execution.** No jobs and no POST execution: the links with rel `http://www.opengis.net/def/rel/ogc/1.0/execute` are the mode's tile endpoints, templated (`{z}`, `{x}`, `{y}`), with the inputs as query parameters. `POST /processes/{processId}/execution` answers 501 with those links.

get.summary: Read a Terrain Viewer share link: which modes it shows
get.description:
Turns a link of the app (the address the Share dialog copies, `https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/?...`) into what this service needs to draw the same view: the modes it switches on (`active`), every mode's opacity (`opacity`: its own times its group's), the parameters every layer keeps (`params`: the terrain source, ramps, light...), the camera (`camera`: lat, lng, zoom, when the link has them) and the tile addresses that draw it (`tiles.terrain`, an XYZ template of the active modes; `tiles.basemap` when the link shows imagery). The QGIS plugin's *Open link* reads it to add the view's layers.

**Ways to ask.** Give the whole link as `url` (URL-encoded): `/view?url=https%3A%2F%2Fterrain-viewer.iconem.com%2F%3FshowTerrainAnalysis%3Dtrue%26slopeOpacity%3D0.5%26terrainSourceA%3Dmapterhorn`; `url` can also be only the link's query, with or without its `?`. Or paste the link's query (what follows `?`) after `/view?`: `/view?showTerrainAnalysis=true&slopeOpacity=0.5&terrainSourceA=mapterhorn`. Or paste the whole link after `/view?`, unencoded: `/view?https://terrain-viewer.iconem.com/?showTerrainAnalysis=true&slopeOpacity=0.5`. A `#...` is ignored; the link's values win over parameters given beside it.

**What comes back** for that link (shortened): `{"active": ["slope", "hillshade"], "opacity": {"slope": 0.5, "hillshade": 1, ...}, "params": {"terrainSource": "mapterhorn"}, "camera": {}, "tiles": {"terrain": "http://localhost:3400/terrain-tiles/mapterhorn/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?modes=slope,hillshade"}}`. Each active mode is a process (`/processes/{id}`) with its settings.
